title: Linux Page Reclaim：file/anon 页、LRU 与 MGLRU
key_conclusions: Page reclaim cost depends on page type: clean file pages are cheap, dirty file pages require writeback, and anonymous pages may require ZRAM swap.
LRU and MGLRU are page-selection mechanisms; vmstat, PSI, and Perfetto are needed to judge whether reclaim is healthy or harmful.
Direct reclaim is more user-visible than background kswapd reclaim because allocation threads pay the stall cost.
Refault and PSI evidence are required to distinguish useful cache reclaim from thrashing.
shallow_points: The article does not include real vmstat, PSI, ZRAM, or Perfetto samples from a device.
It does not validate MGLRU availability and metrics across Android kernels.
It does not include a controlled workload showing clean file reclaim versus anon swap pressure.
It does not quantify practical thresholds for healthy reclaim versus thrashing.
